title: Countable-dimensional modules over the continuous endomorphism algebra are reconstructed from a rank-one corner
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with its extended norm [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $V\ne0$ be a normed $E$-vector space and fix an algebraic basis $(b_j)_{j\in J}$ (every vector has a unique finite linear expansion), with $0\in J$, where $J=\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$ for some $d\geq1$ or $J=\mathbf N$. Suppose constants $0<c\leq C<\infty$ bound the norm of every finite linear combination between $c\max_j|a_j|$ and $C\max_j|a_j|$. Give $V$ its norm topology. Let $D=\operatorname{End}^{\mathrm{cts}}_E(V)$ be the unital $E$-algebra of all continuous $E$-linear endomorphisms, with multiplication given by composition. Write $\lambda_0:V\to E$ for the $b_0$-coordinate and $e(v)=\lambda_0(v)b_0$, a continuous idempotent of rank one. If $H$ is any unital left $D$-module whose induced $E$-vector space is algebraically spanned by at most countably many elements, put $eH=\{eh:h\in H\}$. Then the specified map
$$V\otimes_E eH\longrightarrow H,\qquad v\otimes h\longmapsto \theta_v h,\qquad\theta_v(w)=\lambda_0(w)v,$$
is an isomorphism of left $D$-modules, where $D$ acts on the first tensor factor. No topology or continuity assumption is imposed on $H$. The assertion includes $H=0$ and finite-dimensional $V$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary: rank-one reconstruction using the finite-rank ideal and an uncountable almost-disjoint family of coordinate subsets. Exact reference WANTED; intended proof in report.md.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-bounded-coordinate-split-projections] with $K=E$, the given basis and $j_0=0$. Its hypotheses are exactly the two norm bounds. We obtain the continuous coordinates, all matrix units $E_{ij}$, their multiplication identities, and the specified continuous operators $\theta_v$. In particular the algebra $D$, viewed as a subalgebra of $\operatorname{End}_E(V)$, contains every matrix unit.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary: assembly of the three extracted arguments; returned proof steps 1–10.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-matrix-unit-corner-embedding] to this subalgebra and $H$. It gives precisely the specified injective $D$-linear map $\Phi:V\otimes_E eH\to H$. Its image $N$ is $D$-stable, and $Q=H/N$ is annihilated by $e$ and every $E_{jj}$. The image in $Q$ of the given at most countable spanning family of $H$ spans $Q$, so $Q$ is countably spanned.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary: assembly of the three extracted arguments; returned proof steps 1–10.

proof.text: If $J$ is finite, evaluation on the basis gives $1_D=\sum_{j\in J}E_{jj}$. Every summand annihilates $Q$, so its identity acts as zero and $Q=0$. This includes $d=1$. Hence it remains to handle $J=\mathbf N$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary: assembly of the three extracted arguments; returned proof steps 1–10.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-uncountable-almost-disjoint-family] to obtain uncountable $I$ and infinite $A_i\subseteq\mathbf N$ with finite pairwise intersections. By [lem-sfb-bounded-coordinate-split-projections], each $A_i$ gives $u_i,r_i,p_i\in D$ with $r_iu_i=1_D$, $p_i=u_ir_i$ and, for $i\ne j$, $p_ip_j=\sum_{k\in A_i\cap A_j}E_{k0}eE_{0k}$. For $x\in Q$, $E_{0k}x\in Q$ and $e(E_{0k}x)=0$ by step 2, so every summand kills $x$. Thus $(p_ip_j)Q=0$, as an assertion about the action on $Q$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary: assembly of the three extracted arguments; returned proof steps 1–10.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-orthogonal-split-idempotents-small-module] with $K=E$, the unital algebra $D$, the countably spanned module $Q$, and these $u_i,r_i$. The index set is uncountable, and the products $p_ip_j$ annihilate $Q$ for distinct indices by step 4. Its final clause gives $Q=0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary: assembly of the three extracted arguments; returned proof steps 1–10.

proof.text: In both cases $H/N=0$ implies $N=H$, so $\Phi$ is surjective as well as injective. Its inverse is $D$-linear: for $y=\Phi(z)$, the equation $\Phi(Tz)=Ty$ and uniqueness of a preimage give $\Phi^{-1}(Ty)=Tz$. This is the claimed isomorphism with $D$ acting on the first tensor factor. When $H=0$, the source and target are both zero and the same argument applies.
